intro.TrustedMarkup:
One comment- and string-aware cursor over foreign text (CSS, ICU messages, HTML templates, SDL) for generators.

Offsets are byte offsets. The scanner is a record advanced through modify functions, which keep line/col in sync. until, untilStr and balanced skip over quoted strings and line and block comments, so a delimiter inside one never ends the scan. Block comments do not nest: the first blockClose closes one, as in CSS and C.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type Scanner = { src: String, pos: Int64, line: Int64, col: Int64, // The line-comment marker ("//", "#", ...); "" disables line comments. lineComment: String, // The block-comment open/close markers ("/*" and "*/" for CSS); "" for // `blockOpen` disables block comments. Non-nesting. blockOpen: String, blockClose: String, // Primary and secondary quote bytes (34 for ", 39 for '); -1 disables. quote1: Int64, quote2: Int64, // The escape byte inside a quoted string (92 for backslash); -1 disables. escape: Int64, }

prose.TrustedMarkup: A cursor over src, with 1-based line/col and its lexical config.
A Vyrn-flavored scanner: // line comments, "/' strings, \ escape. Vyrn has no block comments, so blockOpen/blockClose are disabled.
A CSS-flavored scanner: no line comments, /* */ block comments, "/' strings, \ escape.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn scanner( src: String, lineComment: String, blockOpen: String, blockClose: String, quote1: Int64, quote2: Int64, escape: Int64, ) -> Scanner

prose.TrustedMarkup: A fully configured scanner. Pass "" for lineComment/blockOpen to disable that comment kind and -1 for any disabled byte.
The current byte, or -1 at end of input.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn peekAt(sc: Scanner, n: Int64) -> Int64

prose.TrustedMarkup: The byte n ahead, or -1 past the end.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn looksAt(sc: Scanner, s: String) -> Bool

prose.TrustedMarkup: Whether the input at the cursor begins with s.
Consumes a [A-Za-z0-9_]+ run and returns it (empty if none here).

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn quotedString(sc: modify Scanner) -> Option<String>

prose.TrustedMarkup: If the cursor is at a quote, consumes the quoted run and returns its inner text with escapes as written; the caller decodes its own dialect. None if not at a quote. An unterminated string returns the text to end of input.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn until(sc: modify Scanner, stop: Int64) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: Consumes up to, not including, the first top-level byte stop, skipping quoted strings and comments, and returns the consumed text. Stops at end of input if stop never appears at the top level.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn untilStr(sc: modify Scanner, stop: String) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: Like until, but for the multi-byte string stop. The cursor is left on stop.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn balanced(sc: modify Scanner, open: Int64, close: Int64) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: With the cursor at byte open, consumes the balanced region through the matching close (nesting, string and comment aware) and returns the text between them. An unbalanced region returns everything to end of input. Not at open: returns "" and consumes nothing.
